headline: Bitcoin swung from below $76,000 to above $80,000 on Wednesday as markets digested the Democrats' sweep of Congress, and House Democrats have begun discussing their own crypto market-structure bill.

market.asOf: Read from the CoinMarketCap homepage about 19:56 UTC Wed 4 Nov (02:56 Thu Bangkok). The 24-hour change could not be read with its direction, so it is left out. CoinGecko showed bitcoin at $80,244.70 at almost the same moment, about $2,000 higher, so the two sources disagree. For current prices, use the live prices on this page.
market.fearGreed: 34 (Fear) on the Alternative.me Crypto Fear & Greed Index, up from 26 yesterday, read about 19:55 UTC 4 Nov. CoinMarketCap's own index read 37 (Fear).

stories.title: Bitcoin's midterm whipsaw: from under $76,000 to above $80,000
stories.summary: Bitcoin fell to a seven-week low overnight as results showed Democrats winning both chambers of Congress, then bounced back above $80,000 once Wall Street opened and stocks rallied. Traders who had bet on further falls were forced to buy back, speeding up the move. Money was still leaving US bitcoin funds earlier in the week.
points: Bitcoin's overnight low was $75,618, its weakest in seven weeks, per TheStreet.
By 12:06 p.m. ET bitcoin was about $80,450, up 3.65% over 24 hours; the Nasdaq was up 2.15% and the S&P 500 1.9%, per CoinDesk.
$378M of short bets were liquidated in one hour, and $914.8M of positions in 24 hours, per CoinGlass data cited by crypto.news.
US bitcoin ETFs lost about $1.16B over three sessions to 3 Nov, per SoSoValue data cited by Cointelegraph; Bitwise calls the selling short-term.
Bitcoin is still about 41% below its record above $122,000 from October 2025, per Reuters.

stories.title: Democrats control Congress and are discussing their own crypto bill
stories.summary: With Democrats taking both chambers, the industry-backed CLARITY Act looks less likely to pass this year. House Democrats have begun discussing their own market-structure bill for the new Congress that would give the SEC a bigger role, and plan to investigate the Trump family's crypto businesses.
points: CLARITY failed a Senate procedural vote 49-50 in September, short of the 60 needed; a prediction market gives it a 3% chance of becoming law in 2026, per Decrypt.

The ideas under discussion would give the SEC a bigger supervisory role and narrow the CFTC's, and would likely address crypto activities of the president and other federal officials, per crypto.news.
Maxine Waters is likely to return as chair of the House Financial Services Committee, per The Block.
House Democrats plan to investigate Trump family crypto businesses, starting with World Liberty Financial, per Bitcoin Magazine.

stories.title: Security crisis: a French bank theft of over $133M and Binance hackers still moving funds
stories.summary: Crédit Mutuel Arkéa told CoinDesk an attack enabled fraudulent transactions and is now under control, without giving an amount; investigator ZachXBT puts losses above $133M. Separately, the hackers behind Binance's breach have moved most of the stolen SOL, and Binance users pulled billions after the exchange reopened.
points: ZachXBT's estimate is over $133M: $106M first reported on 2 Nov plus $27M more, and it could be higher, per CoinDesk.
Bitquery traced $108.8M in USDC withdrawn from Kraken, Crypto.com and OKX over 21 hours, per CoinDesk.
Binance attackers have moved about 81% of 970,522 stolen SOL, routing it through THORChain into bitcoin, per Cointelegraph.
The FBI attributes the Binance attack to North Korea's TraderTraitor group, per Cointelegraph.
Binance users withdrew a net $4.72B on Tuesday after the exchange reopened, per Reuters.

briefs.title: Block faces a $764M DOJ settlement
briefs.summary: Block agreed in principle to pay $764M to settle a DOJ anti-money-laundering probe, and its bitcoin gross profit fell 50% to $52M, per CoinDesk.

briefs.title: Bernstein cuts bitcoin miner targets
briefs.summary: Bernstein cut price targets on seven miners after Democrats won the Texas governor's race, citing risk to AI data-center plans; Riot went from $35 to $18, per CoinDesk.

briefs.title: Riot signs a 15-year AI lease
briefs.summary: Riot shares rose 14% on a $28B, 15-year AI lease for its Corsicana, Texas campus; it held 2,418 BTC at quarter end, per CoinDesk.

briefs.title: Circle Q3 revenue up, staff cut
briefs.summary: Circle's Q3 revenue rose 17% to $865M, per CoinDesk, and it is cutting about 5% of staff, per TheStreet.

briefs.title: US hiring and services data
briefs.summary: ADP private payrolls rose 86,000 in October against 69,000 expected, and the ISM services index was 54.5 against 54.8 expected, per CoinDesk.

briefs.title: CFTC clears stock perpetual futures
briefs.summary: The CFTC cleared perpetual futures on stocks, a product borrowed from crypto trading, per CoinDesk; a group backed by Cboe and Citadel Securities has sued, per crypto.news.

briefs.title: SEC no-action letter for Canton Coin
briefs.summary: An SEC division treated Canton Coin as a digital commodity in a no-action letter, per The Block.
